quotes.text: Think of it as a two-way mirror, a live connection between your device and Microsoft servers, where any change on one side automatically shows up on the other
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear image that corrects the myth that sync is just uploading.

quotes.text: If you delete an online only file from your device, it deletes it from OneDrive everywhere. It's gone from the cloud, too.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical warning that prevents accidental data loss.

quotes.text: The sync engine is reliable, but it follows rules. When you break those rules, it breaks silently. There's no pop-up, no warning, just a red X on the OneDrive icon
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why sync failures often go unnoticed.

quotes.text: A lot of people think selective sync and files on demand do the same thing. They don't. There are two different tools that solve two different problems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up a common confusion between two OneDrive features.

quotes.text: One drive sync isn't complicated. It follows rules, learn those rules and it works flawlessly. Break them and you get the red X.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's core message in three sentences.

takeaways: OneDrive sync is a continuous two-way mirror between devices and the cloud, backed by version history, not a one-time upload.
Files On-Demand keeps all files visible as online-only placeholders, while selective sync decides which folders appear on a device at all.
Most sync problems come from long paths, full storage, locked files or unsupported characters, and pausing and resuming sync fixes many temporary glitches.
hook: Most people think OneDrive is just a cloud folder - until files vanish or sync gets stuck with a red X. This episode explains in plain English how the sync engine, Files On-Demand and selective sync really work and why sync breaks. Everyday Microsoft 365 users learn simple habits to keep sync healthy and see how Copilot is turning OneDrive into a smart assistant.
